ModMetaData.name: RimAgent
ModMetaData.author: mushroomTW
ModMetaData.description:
RimAgent — an in-game AI agent for RimWorld colony management.
Open the Agent window and issue commands in natural language. RimAgent inspects the colony through 82 specialized tools, executes only authorized game actions, and logs every invocation.
Requires RimLLM Framework 2026.10.20.1 or later (must be loaded before RimAgent). Configure model providers, API credentials, models, and fallback chains in RimLLM Framework; RimAgent provides colony tools and category permission controls.
Key Capabilities: • 82 Colony Tools across 16 Categories: Observation (including colonist thoughts, needs, ASCII grid maps, and screenshots), Work priorities and schedules (with /undo), Build (designations and blueprints), Combat, Trade, Medical, Prisoners, Animals, Zones, Production, Time, MCP, Web search, Memory, Subagents, and Save checkpoints. • Four Execution Modes: Confirm (previews every action for player approval), Execute (runs routine tasks directly; confirms major actions), Auto (automated safety review evaluating risk and player intent, rejecting unrequested actions with reasons), and Full access (direct tool execution). • Decision Model Support (Optional): Configure a decision model in RimLLM Framework for fast, cost-effective Auto mode risk checks, independent /goal completion audits, and automatic task category routing. • Autonomous Colony Care: Optional background monitoring reacting to raids, mental break risks, food shortages, injuries, and fires, combined with periodic colony patrols and exponential backoff retries. • Persistent Goals (/goal): Queue multi-step objectives that persist across save files and execute incrementally until verified complete or paused. • Subagents & Model Roles: Delegate tasks to isolated subagents (parallel read-only execution) and assign dedicated models and reasoning levels to subagents, classifiers, and /compact summaries. • Dual-Scope Memory: Global memory (prefixed with global_) shared across all saves, alongside save-specific colony memory notes. • MCP Extensibility: Connect trusted local Model Context Protocol servers to provide custom external tools.
Safety Notices: • Combat orders experience several seconds of latency due to LLM round-trip time; designed for strategic positioning and retreats rather than micro-tactics. • Local MCP servers run with your operating system user privileges; only connect servers you trust.
